quotes.text: derived from real clinical records in the STAnford Research Repository (STARR)

rationale: The source is named (STARR, plus the e-consult system) and the release is a versioned Docker image on Redivis (physicianbench-fhir-v1). No snapshot date or time frame of the records is given, and no route from a task to its source record is stated, so the level-2 elements are missing.

quotes.text: specifically from the e-consult system in which primary care providers submit structured referral questions to subspecialists

rationale: Origin (de-identified STARR e-consult records) and collection/selection method (185-case pool, complexity filter) are stated. No licence or data terms (README only says 'See LICENSE') and no consent or IRB statement appear in S1-S3, so only origin plus one other element is present.

quotes.text: E-consult records were selected to span diverse subspecialties and task types

rationale: A sampling design is stated (selection to span subspecialties and task types, complexity filter) and task distributions are tabulated (Tables A1, A2). No comparison of patient features against a named target population is reported.

quotes.text: including consistency with retrieved data, adherence to clinical guidelines, and absence of clinically unsafe recommendations

rationale: Documentation checkpoints assess absence of clinically unsafe recommendations, so an unsafe-output criterion exists, though it is part of a documentation rubric rather than a dedicated suite. No bias test is reported; borderline between 0 and 1.

searched: S1 (abstract, Sec 3-6, Appendix A-G), S2 (README), S3 (empty), S4/S5. No gating, canary, encryption, held-out split or overlap check is reported. Record perturbation and note rewriting are described only as privacy measures.
searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. Per-task containers isolate state across evaluations, but no statement says the agent cannot reach ground truth or the grader at run time, and no mechanism is named.

quotes.text: ensuring exact reproducibility without any runtime data ingestion

rationale: Data and FHIR server are pinned in a self-contained Docker image (v1). LLM-judge and hybrid graders call a live model whose identity and version are not given in S1-S3, so the evaluator is unpinned.

quotes.text: a reference solution summary and review checklist supporting structured physician validation

rationale: Only manual evidence: physicians review each task's solution summary and checkpoints against the EHR over multiple rounds. No scripted reference solution is run through the grader and no result is reported.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. Tasks change state (orders, prescriptions, appointments, messages), so the item applies. Code graders only look for the expected created resources among agent-authored ones; no check that unrelated state is unchanged or that extra writes are penalised is reported.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. No random or trivial-agent rate, chance rate per metric, or design argument that trivial outputs fail is given. The lowest model scores (5.3-6.0%) are reported as results, not as a chance baseline.
searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. No do-nothing or random-agent result is reported for any task.

quotes.text: checkpoint validity (whether evaluation criteria are appropriate and complete)

rationale: Physicians review the checkpoints and grading criteria, which is validation without figures. There are no agreement or error figures for the LLM-judge or hybrid graders on benchmark outputs, and no reference-solution or test evidence for the code graders in S1-S3. Weak 1.

quotes.text: For models that support a reasoning-effort parameter, we set it to high and run 3 independent trials to compute the reliability metrics.

rationale: S1 states 3 independent trials and a fixed reasoning effort, but agent temperature is the provider default and no seed is given. Judge temperature 0 appears only in code (S4), so the safeguards are partial.

Table 2 reports a spread (\pm) on Pass@1 but does not define it. The text claims GPT-5.5 'leads by a wide margin' with absolute gaps, and no CI or significance test is applied to the headline comparison.

quotes.text: For models that support a reasoning-effort parameter, we set it to high and run 3 independent trials to compute the reliability metrics.

rationale: Run count (3 per task), decoding controls (provider-default temperature, reasoning effort high) and independence of runs are all stated in S1. No explicit seed, but the anchor accepts decoding controls. element_flags 3/3.

A \pm spread is given on Pass@1 headline scores, though it is not stated whether it is SE, SD or CI. The resampling unit (task, run) is not named, and clustering of tasks within patients or specialty groups is not addressed. element_flags 1/3.

quotes.text: Pass^3 ( Yao et al., 2025 ) =c^{k}/n^{k} estimates the probability that all k runs succeed, measuring consistency and reliability.

rationale: Pass^3, an all-runs metric, is defined and reported per model over 3 independent runs (best 28.0%). No action-sequence or end-state agreement across reruns is reported. element_flags 1/3, scored 2 under the item anchors.

quotes.text: For models that support a reasoning-effort parameter, we set it to high and run 3 independent trials to compute the reliability metrics.

contradiction_quotes.text: We allow up to 100 tool-calling turns per task

rationale: Decoding parameters (default temperature, reasoning effort high, 100-step cap) are stated. Models are named by family and version only, with no snapshot ID or release date, and no harness tag or commit is tied to the reported numbers. The single-task runner defaults to 200 steps and the MiniAgent class to 30, against the reported 100; candidate flag only. element_flags 1/3.

quotes.text: All tools accept structured parameters following the function-calling schema
Search tools issue GET requests against the FHIR server; create tools issue POST requests that persist on the task-local server.
caught and returned to the model as a structured {"error": ...} message rather than propagating
Use the FHIR create tools to place orders, send messages, or schedule appointments.

rationale: JSON schemas for all 14 tools, read vs write semantics (GET vs POST), return values and structured error returns are documented in S1 (Sec 3.2, Table A4, Appendix E). In S5, the tool descriptions and system prompt separate 'search' from 'create' tools, so read/write reaches the agent. element_flags 3/3.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. No tests or conformance checks of the tools are reported, and no statement says whether any tool behaviour (for example Communication create or Appointment create) is stubbed or live. Nothing reaches S5. element_flags 0/3.

quotes.text: write actions (e.g., creating a MedicationRequest ) modify the EHR state, while read actions (e.g., searching for lab results) leave it unchanged
create tools issue POST requests that persist on the task-local server

rationale: Write actions are identified and shown as executed against a task-local, fresh-container FHIR server. S5 descriptions name 'create' tools but never say writes are sandboxed or executed. No scoring or penalty for unsafe or unnecessary writes is reported; only note content is checked for unsafe recommendations. element_flags 2/3.

quotes.text: code graders query the FHIR server to verify that the agent created the expected resources
evaluate aspects of clinical reasoning and documentation that resist purely programmatic assessment

rationale: Grader inputs are stated (post-execution FHIR state for code graders, agent free-text for hybrid and LLM-judge), and the LLM-judge use is justified. No validation of graders on labelled correct and incorrect outcomes with error rates is reported. element_flags 2/3.

quotes.text: A fresh container is provisioned per task and torn down after evaluation, so no state leaks across evaluations.

rationale: Cross-task state leakage is controlled by per-task fresh containers, and the agent has only FHIR and file-write tools with a minimal system prompt. No held-out or private split is reported (tasks and tests are public) and no canary or provenance marker is given. element_flags 1/3.

quotes.text: Table 3: Pass@1 (%) by clinical specialty group.
Diagnosis & Interpretation (N=13) | Result Interpretation | 9

rationale: Results are given per specialty group (Table 3) and per task type (Table A5), with task counts per type and subspecialty in Tables A1-A2. Source records hold demographic fields (age, sex), yet no per-patient-subgroup results are reported. element_flags 2/3.

quotes.text: a de-identified clinical data warehouse linked to Stanford Health Care EHR systems
were replaced with synthetically generated values using the Faker library

rationale: Records are stated as real de-identified STARR data, with a described de-identification method (perturbation, Faker, HIPAA Safe Harbor-style note scrubbing). No IRB or DUA is named, and no data terms separate from the code licence ('See LICENSE') appear in S1-S3. element_flags 2/3.
